entries.status: Live on mainnet / alpha
entries.title: Lightning Labs ships Wavelength on mainnet: bitcoin payments any agent can integrate
entries.summary: Wavelength, Lightning Labs' payments toolkit, opened to everyone on mainnet October 23. An agent can hold a balance and pay for API calls, data feeds or another agent's service in fractions of a cent over Lightning - no card, account, node or channels. wavecli mcp serve exposes the wallet as MCP tool calls; L402 handles pay-per-request APIs.
entries.detail: This is the closest shipping thing to the SatStacker payment lane. It is still alpha: accounts are capped at 300,000 sats (50,000 per VTXO), Lightning payments carry a 0.25% service fee plus routing fees, and stablecoins are only 'coming soon' per Lightning Labs. The custody shape is the interesting part: users hold their own keys with a unilateral exit back to the bitcoin chain, wallet unlock stays on the command line so seeds never cross the agent channel, and receive-only macaroon credentials let an agent get paid with no ability to sign or recover. Funds need a refresh roughly every two weeks, handled automatically while the wallet runs. Fee and cap figures are Lightning Labs' own documentation, checked October 24.

entries.status: Live feature / reported
entries.title: Coinbase opens customer accounts to AI agents over MCP
entries.summary: Coinbase announced 'Coinbase is open for AI agents' on October 22: users can connect approved assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Codex CLI and others) through its MCP server to trade crypto, US stocks and derivatives. The user picks which portfolios the agent can access, previews orders before execution, and can disconnect at any time.
entries.detail: Reported by Yahoo Finance / 24/7 Wall St on October 23. The setup is agents.coinbase.com/mcp as a custom MCP server with an approval screen; a September update had already added stocks, ETFs and x402 payments that let agents buy market data from a user's USDC balance. Coinbase's own risk framing matches what this watch keeps repeating: fund only a separate, limited portfolio for agent trading, because the named failure modes are prompt injection, the agent misreading vague instructions, and over-broad permissions. Coinbase has reported no agent revenue so far and gave no usage numbers. Feature claims are Coinbase's; the risk framing is the article's.

entries.status: Disclosed / fixed in the August 18 releases
entries.title: x402 SDK flaw let a malicious API ask an agent's wallet for its full token balance
entries.summary: Security firm V12 disclosed 25 flaws in the x402 payment SDKs, three critical: the default client set no spending limit (a hostile API could request the wallet's full token balance), the TypeScript Solana facilitator accepted token approvals as valid payments, and SIWx login messages were not checked against the site actually contacted. All three were fixed in the August 18 releases, which cap payments at $1 and recognized stablecoins by default.
entries.detail: The uncomfortable part is the disclosure gap: the x402 Foundation published no security advisories and the changelogs do not call the fixes security fixes, so npm audit and PyPI gave no warning to upgrade - teams on releases before 2.23.0 (TS) or 2.25.0 (Python) have to find out some other way. Neither V12 nor the foundation reports any real-world exploit. The design lesson is the SatStacker one: any agent that auto-signs payments needs explicit per-payment budgets, token allowlists and site verification, which is exactly what the fixed clients now ship. Technical claims are V12's as reported by The Hacker News, checked October 24.

sources.label: The Hacker News on the V12 findings

entries.status: Single-author experiment / backtest results
entries.title: An LLM agent searched for trading strategies; a simple heuristic beat it, and the harness was the real hero
entries.summary: Pavel Kazantsev gave DeepSeek V3 forty rounds to propose crypto strategies, scored by a walk-forward harness the model could not touch. A dumb heuristic proposer found +52% net first; the agent's early proposals lost money; its real value was surfacing three silent harness bugs; and its later +123.7% 'win' turned out to be parameter sensitivity, not edge.
entries.detail: The details matter more than the headline. The agent never touched scoring - it proposed, the same judge every hand-built strategy faced decided. Once the space was debugged it genuinely mapped a corner (factor-residual reversion, 40-80 day lookbacks), but the honest ensemble result was +75.8% in-sample with a t-stat around 1.4: not significant. His conclusions read like a checklist for the deterministic-core design: run a heuristic baseline first; the agent is only as honest as the thing that scores it; once a proposer can optimize it will, so watch breadth, not magnitude; average the plateau instead of picking the winner. A personal blog experiment with the author's own caveats, not peer-reviewed research - but unusually rigorous about its own search bias.

entries.status: Exchange feature / promo stage
entries.title: Binance pushes agent wallets with claimable '.ai' Agent ID names
entries.summary: Binance co-founder Yi He is promoting Agent ID - unique '.ai' names for Binance Wallet's agentic wallet, pitched as an alternative to long 0x addresses. It sits on the August Agent OS platform: MCP integration, isolated agent subaccounts for spot, margin and futures trading, and no external-withdrawal permission for agents.
entries.detail: Neither promo post shows an actual payment or trade completed through the names, so treat this as a naming launch on top of real plumbing. The plumbing is the part worth watching: a dedicated subaccount, isolated from the main account, where the agent can trade but cannot withdraw externally - the exchange-custodied version of the least-privilege pattern Wavelength ships self-custodied. Caveat for a California-based stack: Binance's global platform is not available to US residents, so this is a pattern to study rather than a tool to use. Reported by crypto.news October 20.

entries.status: Live in Grok Bot marketplace / vendor-described guardrails
entries.title: MetaMask Agent Wallet goes live on Grok Bot with wallet-layer guardrails
entries.summary: MetaMask's Agent Wallet is available as a Grok Bot marketplace plugin as of October 28: plain-language requests can check balances, swap and bridge tokens, trade Hyperliquid perps, take Polymarket positions and supply to yield vaults. MetaMask says the wallet is self-custodial with keys in a trusted execution environment, every supported transaction simulated and Blockaid-scanned, and Guard Mode enforcing allowlists plus a rolling 24-hour outflow limit you set, with two-factor approval for anything outside it.
entries.detail: The structurally important detail is where the checks fire: swaps are checked trade by trade, but perp positions are checked only at the Hyperliquid deposit - opening, sizing and closing positions are Hyperliquid-signed actions, so a position well past the outflow limit can open without a wallet-level check. Polymarket order placement is likewise off-chain and outside per-order Guard Mode evaluation. A 'Beast Mode' relaxes interruptions while keeping threat scanning, and eligible transactions carry Transaction Protection coverage up to $10,000 a month. The same mm CLI skill works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other skill-supporting agents. All of this is MetaMask's own documentation, not independent testing. Not investment advice.

entries.status: Launched per vendor / MCP private beta
entries.title: Tria launches agentic perp trading with trade-only keys
entries.summary: Tria announced Agentic Trading on October 30: AI tools including Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor execute Hyperliquid and Decibel perpetual-futures strategies through a user's existing Tria account, authorized through expiring, revocable trade-only keys that cannot withdraw funds. Tria's own documentation qualifies the launch: the MCP server is in access-restricted private beta, and both venues trade real mainnet markets with no testnet target. This is perp execution, not a verified native ZEC/ADA or spot bitcoin-DCA product.
entries.detail: Mechanics per the docs: users mint an HL agent wallet and/or a Decibel delegate keypair from the Tria app; agents place, cancel and modify orders but cannot withdraw. Tria's risk disclosure states trade-only permissions do not prevent trading losses, including liquidation of collateral. The 600,000-user figure and named AI-tool support are vendor claims, and usable availability is gated on private-beta npm access. Also covered in this hub's blockchain chapter. Not investment advice.

entries.status: Published release / maintainer-described fixes
entries.title: Wavelength v0.2.1 hardens the BTC agent-payment rail
entries.summary: Lightning Labs published Wavelength v0.2.1 on October 31. The release validates Ark transaction inputs before accepting out-of-round transfers, repairs VTXO expiry monitoring, rejects excessive refund timelocks before funding pay swaps, and improves swap refunds, unilateral exits and fee-bump recovery. This is payment infrastructure for the SatStacker lane, not a bitcoin accumulation strategy.
entries.detail: Linux builds disable MPTCP listeners by default; the release explicitly says this mitigation does not replace installing a patched kernel. Operators must provide complete, co-signed Ark transaction packages, and applications must treat a zero indexed-expiry deadline as unverified timing. These are maintainer-described fixes, not an independent security audit or evidence of a loss in the wild. The published release body retains draft/signing boilerplate, so this check does not certify every binary signature. Wavelength is a separate repository from lightning-agent-tools; its release should not be inferred from the companion repository's older push date. No software installed, keys connected or funds moved.

entries.type: Exchange agents / Guardrails / rolling out, with one feature marked coming soon
entries.status: Official announcement / server-side controls, not an agent-side promise
entries.title: Coinbase adds server-side Agent Controls for agentic trading
entries.summary: Coinbase says Agent Controls are rolling out for Coinbase for Agents: maximum trade size, 24-hour volume limits and an auto-stop tied to a portfolio loss threshold. Product permissions for crypto, equities, derivatives and more are marked coming soon. Coinbase says the controls run on its servers and can be changed only from the logged-in app or web account, so the agent cannot rewrite its own limits.
entries.detail: This is the right trust boundary for exchange-connected agents: policy lives with the venue account, not in prompt text. The announced controls still do not make a model's thesis reliable, and a 24-hour volume cap or portfolio auto-stop does not guarantee execution quality, stop fills or protection from gaps. Coinbase's own risk note says agents may make mistakes or fail and that users direct and assume risk for agent transactions and third-party AI provider data use. Availability was not tested in an account. Not investment advice.

entries.status: Reported release with public SDK evidence; setup and app behavior not tested
entries.title: Ledger Agent Intent 0.4.0 adds token approvals for agent-prepared swaps
entries.summary: Exchange.news reports that Ledger Agent Intent 0.4.0 adds template prompts, a smoother first-agent flow and token-approval support on swaps. The model remains proposal-first: an agent prepares an intent, and the owner approves or rejects it on a Ledger signer. Ledger's public agent-intent-sdk repository now has v0.2.0 code for parsing and constraining ERC-20 swap approvals.
entries.detail: Token approvals are the sensitive part of a swap: they authorize a spender contract, often before the swap itself. Ledger's SDK code exposes checks for the sold token, spender, allowance amount, Permit2 and zero-address cases, which is useful evidence that approval handling is explicit rather than hidden. The beta still requires device review and does not prove that a third-party swap quote, provider or agent description is safe. This card intentionally links the report and code, not an enrollment flow; verify the current official Ledger app and domain before connecting an agent. No wallet, signer or transaction was tested.

entries.type: Trading bots / Vendor launch / reported, not tested
entries.status: Press coverage of vendor claims; no live account check
entries.title: Origami Tech says its AI Portfolio Manager can coordinate user-selected trading bots
entries.summary: BlockchainReporter coverage says Origami Tech launched an AI Portfolio Manager that coordinates crypto strategies selected by the user. The agent can switch between strategies, adjust permitted bot parameters and stop a bot when a user-set risk threshold is reached. Earlier stages answer portfolio questions and turn natural-language strategy descriptions into Lua code shown for review.
entries.detail: The useful pattern is bounded orchestration around deterministic bots: the agent does not have to invent order math if the selected strategies and Lua templates define execution. The claims come from vendor-facing coverage, not an independent account test. Strategy switching can still amplify losses, generated Lua needs code review, exchange API scopes and bot permissions were not checked, and a balance stop does not guarantee a fill during gaps or illiquid markets. Not investment advice.

entries.type: Research / Paper / hybrid LLM and rules
entries.status: arXiv preprint / paper-account evidence, not live-market proof
entries.title: Paper tests a hybrid loop: LLM analysts, momentum sizing and rule-based execution
entries.summary: A November 8 arXiv preprint describes company-news and macro agents feeding structured reports to a coordinator, while momentum-based portfolio construction and rule-based execution handle the trading loop. In a broker-recorded paper account from March 11 to August 28, the authors report 34.5% versus 14.4% for SPY, with a larger maximum drawdown.
entries.detail: This is directly relevant to the deterministic-core question: the LLMs analyze and report, while the portfolio engine and execution keep explicit rules and fallbacks. It is not proof that an LLM has a durable edge. The paper uses a paper account plus retrospective policy replays, raw return came with larger drawdown, code and supporting materials are available on request rather than linked, and the study is equities, not crypto or bitcoin accumulation. Treat the result as a design case to test against rule-only twins, not as a strategy recommendation.

entries.title: WalletConnect for Agents prepares transfers and swaps, while the existing wallet still signs
entries.summary: WalletConnect announced an MCP and HTTP interface for balance checks, transfers and supported Uniswap V3 swaps. The vendor says every transaction still needs the owner to approve in their wallet; the assistant prepares the action rather than taking possession of signing keys. These are not tested here. A wallet signature still requires checking recipient, token, chain and contract, and does not make a malicious connection safe. This is an owner-signed execution pattern, not autonomous trading, a return forecast or a recommendation to connect a wallet.

entries.status: Beta / maker-reported benchmark, not independently reproduced
entries.title: Olas launches an on-chain beta agent, with important limits on token caps and sandboxing
entries.summary: Olas introduced olas-ocb-agent in Pearl Connect for payments, swaps, lending and research. The default is to ask before value-moving calls. Its README makes a narrower promise than a universal wallet budget: the native-token cap does not cap ERC-20 transfers or approvals, and auto-approval mode can let those pass without a prompt. Native Windows lacks the documented OS sandbox.
entries.detail: Olas reports zero fund losses in 263 hidden-attack attempts, 89.9% task completion and about $0.05 per completed task. These are maker-reported benchmark results, not a guarantee: Valory builds the agent and runs OnchainBench. The launch describes Gnosis, Polygon and Robinhood Chain through Pearl Connect; the CLI supports broader configurations, which should not be conflated with that product rollout. Not installed, funded or tested here. The token-cap and platform limits matter more than a headline safety score; this is not a recommendation to use auto-approval or commit funds.

entries.status: Preprint / author-reported experiments
entries.title: Signed but Unbound asks which payment limits the wallet signature actually enforces
entries.summary: A November 19 preprint distinguishes an agent-commerce mandate from the fields enforced by the signed token authorization. The authors analyze 12 configurations and report 31,800 local trials on deployed contract code. In a sample of 26,653 redeemed USDC authorizations on Base, 98.7% used a path that any holder of the signature could redeem.
entries.detail: Bearer redemption is exposure, not observed theft: the paper explicitly says it did not observe preemption or misattribution. Results come from the authors, who also wrote the derivation, attacks and checking logic; the sampled Base windows do not represent all payments. Their MandateLock prototype rejects modified mandates in the reported tests at extra gas cost, but is not a production endorsement. For bounded agents, a permission described in a chat or commerce layer is not automatically enforced by the wallet or settlement contract. Not independently reproduced.

entries.status: Experimental launch / approved US users only
entries.title: Visa Crypto Labs opens an experimental agent wallet that pays OUSD for completed tasks
entries.summary: The Block reports Visa Crypto Labs launched an experimental version of its Visa CLI agent wallet on November 23: approved US users with an eligible Visa card verify an AI agent with that credential, register it in Visa's Agent Directory, and earn OUSD when the agent's task submissions are accepted. The wallet is built on Tempo using the Machine Payments Protocol, and the first integration, Taskmarket, pays in OUSD or USDC on Tempo and Base; its site showed 25-plus open tasks at 10 to 50 OUSD.
entries.detail: This extends Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol from e-commerce into agent wallets and task marketplaces, per Cuy Sheffield's statement. Keep the scope tight: experimental, approved and eligible US users only, rewards depend on buyers accepting work, and OUSD earnings are a task marketplace mechanic, not trading yield. Visa's framing, that agents extend rather than replace a person's productive capacity, is the vendor's own positioning. Not investment advice.

entries.status: Launched / vendor performance claims unverified
entries.title: Solana launches solana.ai, bundling an agent kit, payments and a 24/7 trading agent
entries.summary: crypto.news reports Solana introduced solana.ai on November 23, a platform for autonomous agents to trade, manage wallets and pay for services on its chain. It bundles the Solana Agent Kit, the pay.sh payments tool and Milo, a trading agent described as operating around the clock without human approval per transaction, plus Confidential Compute in devnet beta, with Alibaba Cloud named as a launch partner for agent payments.
entries.detail: The headline performance number, more than 1 million payment-channel updates per second, is Solana's own testing claim, not an independent benchmark. An agent that trades without per-transaction approval shifts the entire control burden to whatever limits were configured up front; the coverage does not describe what those limits are for Milo. Platform launch, not an endorsement; not investment advice.

entries.status: Live feature / terms set by AWS
entries.title: AI agents can now pay AWS Marketplace sellers per request, in dollars on the AWS bill
entries.summary: PPC Land reports AWS Marketplace now supports agentic payments: a developer's agent gets a five-minute payment token and can pay sellers per request in dollars, capped at $10,000 per payment, with charges landing on the ordinary AWS bill and no crypto wallet involved. Tavily is among the first sellers.
entries.detail: Notable because it is the x402-style pay-per-request pattern running entirely in dollars inside a cloud bill, rather than in stablecoins on-chain. The guardrails that exist are AWS's: token lifetime and the per-payment cap. How much AWS keeps per sale is not published. Agent spending limits still sit with the developer's own configuration, as this lane's wallet-safety notes keep stressing.

entries.title: Valory unveils OnchainBench, an open benchmark for how safely agents use crypto wallets
entries.summary: Valory, the company behind Olas, announced OnchainBench on November 26: an open benchmark that tests how safely and reliably AI agents operate crypto wallets. The benchmark site and an Apache-2.0 repository are public.
entries.detail: A benchmark for wallet behavior lands directly on this lane's recurring question, which payment limits a wallet signature actually enforces. Caveats: the methodology is self-published, results are vendor-reported, and the repository is days old with minimal third-party adoption so far, so treat any leaderboard as a starting point rather than an industry verdict.

entries.summary: Jesse published 3.7.0 to PyPI on November 23 and 3.7.1 on November 28, hours before this check. Hummingbot remains v2.18.0 from November 18, Freqtrade remains 2026.10, Nautilus Trader remains 1.231.0 stable with the separate 2.0.0rc9 prerelease, and Turnkey remains v2026.11.4 from November 21 UTC.
entries.detail: BTC lane: Wavelength remains v0.2.1 with only the older rc2 tag, and lightning-agent-tools remains v0.2.5. Condor still has no tagged or published releases, though repository commits continued through November 26. AgentKit's PyPI package remains 0.7.4 from October 2025. All eight stack cards carry fresh November 28 checks and star snapshots. No strategies, accounts or software were changed. Release records, not proof of execution quality or returns.

repoPicks.name: x402-foundation/x402
repoPicks.summary: The open x402 payment standard and SDKs: pay-per-request over HTTP 402, with TypeScript, Python and Go clients and MCP support.
repoPicks.why: The rail most of this week's agent-commerce news runs on. Read the security note in this week's edition before wiring an auto-signing client to it.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0. Default clients older than the August 18 releases (TS 2.23.0) lack spending limits - see this week's security note. Star count is a snapshot, not a trend rank.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: hummingbot/condor
repoPicks.summary: The Hummingbot org's open-source harness for creating and managing AI trading agents.
repoPicks.why: Small and early, but it is the dedicated agent layer on top of the execution framework already in the stack watch - and it was actively pushed this week.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. No tagged releases; treat as pre-release software. Star count is a snapshot, not a trend rank.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: TraderAlice/OpenAlice
repoPicks.summary: 'One-person Wall Street': a local workspace connecting coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, others) to market tools, research workspaces and trading accounts, with staged order proposals.
repoPicks.why: The agent-stages-orders-human-approves pattern, shipped as a product-shaped workspace rather than a bot - close to the owner-signed pilot model in the wallet research.
repoPicks.caveat: AGPL-3.0. Feature claims are the README's; trading-account integrations not tested. Star count is a snapshot, not a trend rank.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: Lumiwealth/lumibot
repoPicks.summary: Python trading framework pitching 'AI agents that actually place the trade': backtests, paper and live trading across twelve broker integrations, plus a BotSpot MCP so coding agents get strategy-building skills.
repoPicks.why: The MCP-for-strategy-building angle is the agentic pattern applied to the whole bot lifecycle, not just execution.
repoPicks.caveat: GPL-3.0. Heavily promotes its managed BotSpot cloud; broker integrations not tested. Star count is a snapshot, not a trend rank.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: solana-foundation/pay
repoPicks.summary: Solana Foundation's CLI for agentic payments, speaking x402, MPP and AP2.
repoPicks.why: Agent payment rails are converging on a few protocols; a foundation-backed CLI that speaks three of them is a cheap way to track that convergence.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. Solana-side tooling; not a BTC rail. Star count is a snapshot, not a trend rank.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: MetaMask/agent-skills
repoPicks.summary: The official skills package that teaches agents (Grok Bot, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to drive MetaMask's mm Agent Wallet CLI - which commands to run and when to stop and ask the human first.
repoPicks.why: The code behind this week's headline: read the skill that defines the agent's guardrail behavior before trusting the marketing.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT, 30 stars checked October 31 - new and small; the wallet-layer enforcement lives in the closed mm CLI, not here. Star count is a snapshot, not a trend rank.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: elizaOS/eliza
repoPicks.summary: The open-source agentic operating system: character-driven agents with plugins for chains, exchanges and messaging, the framework many trading bots are built on.
repoPicks.why: The largest active framework in the agent-trading pile; its plugin ecosystem is where most 'agent trades X' demos start.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT, 19,743 stars checked October 31. Very active but sprawling; plugin quality varies and trading plugins are community code. Star count is a snapshot, not a trend rank.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: getAlby/hub
repoPicks.summary: A self-hosted Lightning node with Nostr Wallet Connect, so agents can hold a budget and pay invoices over your own rails instead of a custodial API.
repoPicks.why: The self-custody counterweight to Wavelength's hosted agent payments - same payment lane, keys at home.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0, 286 stars checked October 31. Running your own node is operational work; NWC permissions need the same scoping discipline as any agent key. Star count is a snapshot, not a trend rank.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: lightninglabs/wavelength
repoPicks.summary: BTC payment toolkit with Ark-style VTXOs, wallet tooling and an MCP server.
repoPicks.why: The BTC-specific pick this edition: read the v0.2.1 validation, expiry and recovery notes before relying on an unattended payment loop.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. Young project; operator and expiry assumptions matter. Release publication is not independent binary/signature verification. Stars are checked snapshots, not trend ranks.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick, not a new-launch claim

repoPicks.name: hummingbot/condor
repoPicks.summary: Telegram/web trading harness over Hummingbot API, with optional AI agents and dry-run support.
repoPicks.why: Closest to the agent-over-execution-core pattern: study permissions and the current production-security guidance before connecting real exchange keys.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. No tagged release; snapshot of active source, not audited or tested by this sweep. Stars are checked snapshots, not trend ranks.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick, not a new-launch claim

repoPicks.name: tkhq/sdk
repoPicks.summary: Turnkey wallet SDKs, with executeSwap V4 and authentication/dependency changes in v2026.11.1.
repoPicks.why: Policy-aware wallet plumbing belongs beside, not inside, a model's trading judgment. The release makes a concrete integration checkpoint.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0. A wallet SDK is not a strategy or guarantee of safe trading; backend policies and permissions need their own review. Stars are checked snapshots, not trend ranks.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick, not a new-launch claim

repoPicks.name: jesse-ai/jesse
repoPicks.summary: Python framework for researching and running deterministic trading strategies; PyPI 3.6.0 published November 3.
repoPicks.why: A research-to-execution core to compare with LLM orchestration, without treating a language model as the risk engine.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. Package publication and repository metrics checked; live execution and strategy performance not tested. Stars are checked snapshots, not trend ranks.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick, not a new-launch claim

repoPicks.name: LedgerHQ/agent-intent-sdk
repoPicks.summary: Headless TypeScript SDK for Ledger Agent Intent enrollment, authentication and signed intent submission; v0.2.0 exports shared ERC-20 swap-approval checks.
repoPicks.why: A direct code view of the hardware-approval model: agents propose signed intents, the owner approves on the signer, and swap token approvals get explicit parsing and refusal rules.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0. Official LedgerHQ repository, but the checked star count was 0, so treat it as new infrastructure rather than community validation. The service is beta; no setup was performed or tested, and any enrollment link should be verified from current official Ledger surfaces.
repoPicks.label: Official SDK / very new, not a production-readiness signal

repoPicks.name: okx/agent-skills
repoPicks.summary: Official Markdown agent skills for the OKX CLI, covering public market data, spot and derivatives orders, portfolio operations, grid and DCA bots, earn products and smart-money data.
repoPicks.why: A concrete exchange-skill pattern: unauthenticated market reads sit beside clearly marked credentialed skills for orders, transfers and bots, so an agent's activation boundary is visible in files.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. Official OKX organization, but no skill was installed or run. OAuth or API credentials, real order permissions, bot settings and exchange jurisdiction remain separate checks; review skill text before loading it into an agent.
repoPicks.label: Official exchange skills / active repo, not an execution endorsement

repoPicks.name: alpacahq/alpaca-mcp-server
repoPicks.summary: Alpaca's official MCP server for stocks, ETFs, crypto, options, portfolio management and market data through Claude, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients.
repoPicks.why: A broker-backed MCP example with a free paper-trading account, useful for testing the boundary between natural-language tool calls and deterministic order APIs before any live trading.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. Version 2 is a breaking rewrite of v1 tool names. Use paper trading first; real orders are possible. The README recommends local stdio and warns not to expose a remote server configured with Alpaca keys.
repoPicks.label: Official broker MCP / paper-test candidate, not a live-trading recommendation

repoPicks.name: HKUDS/Vibe-Trading
repoPicks.summary: Personal trading agent for market research, backtests, paper portfolios and optional broker execution within user-set limits, with multi-source data and quant-research workflows.
repoPicks.why: A broad example of the architecture this lane watches: LLM research and planning feed explicit backtests, paper fills, broker permissions and haltable mandates instead of a free-form model placing trades.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. The README says live broker execution is experimental and not verified by the maintainers against a real broker account. Star count is a snapshot, not a quality score. Model providers, data sources, broker permissions and live limits need separate review.
repoPicks.label: Active agent-trading stack / high-star snapshot, live mode experimental

repoPicks.name: hypurrquant/perp-cli
repoPicks.summary: CLI, MCP server and agent skill for perpetual futures across multiple DEXs, with JSON output, dry-run, testnet, funding-arb tooling, portfolio views, bots and an OWS signing guardrail.
repoPicks.why: A crypto-native, agent-first CLI: structured output, pre-trade validation, slippage bounds, client-order IDs and a policy executable give an agent clearer stop points than an improvised browser flow.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. Very low-star and young. Perpetuals can liquidate quickly, venue and mainnet support varies, and bridge or withdrawal permissions need separate review. No install, keys, order or venue account was tested.
repoPicks.label: Editorial pick / very young low-star repo, high-risk venue category

repoPicks.name: hummingbot/hummingbot
repoPicks.summary: Open-source execution framework for exchange connectivity, market making and systematic strategies.
repoPicks.why: Revisited for stable v2.18.0: execution and backtest fixes plus removal of the unsafe remote-data deserialization path, rather than a generic popularity pick.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0. See the specific release/security note. Paper-mode support depends on the strategy path; do not assume every controller can run without live accounts. No install, code audit or performance test.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial revisit

repoPicks.name: hummingbot/condor
repoPicks.summary: Agent harness around Hummingbot API, including domain agents, custom tick strategies and dry-run support.
repoPicks.why: A direct fit for the SatStacker split between an agent layer and deterministic execution. Revisited with a fresh checked snapshot, not a new release claim.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. No tagged releases. API can control orders, balances and stored exchange credentials; README recommends private networking plus strong credentials. Dry-run is a software feature, not proof of live safety or profits.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial revisit

repoPicks.name: valory-xyz/olas-ocb-agent
repoPicks.summary: Small open-source CLI agent and Pearl Connect beta for on-chain payments, swaps, lending and research.
repoPicks.why: The approval broker and explicit security limits make this more useful to inspect than a headline benchmark alone.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0. Zero stars at check is a fresh snapshot, not a quality verdict. Native-value cap excludes ERC-20 transfers/approvals, which can pass in auto mode; native Windows has no documented OS sandbox. Maker runs the benchmark too. Not installed or funded.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: lightninglabs/wavelength
repoPicks.summary: Bitcoin/Lightning payment tooling for agent-accessible services, with wallet and MCP interfaces.
repoPicks.why: Keeps the BTC payment rail visible in this edition while the week's new launches mostly target EVM wallets. Revisited, not a new stable release.
repoPicks.caveat: MIT. Stable remains v0.2.1; v0.2.2-rc1 is only a tag. Separate from lightning-agent-tools. Wallet operation carries fees, expiry/recovery and custody risks; no funds moved and no software tested.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial revisit

repoPicks.name: TauricResearch/TradingAgents
repoPicks.summary: A multi-agent LLM framework for trading research: analyst, researcher, trader and risk roles debate and decide, paper-trading oriented.
repoPicks.why: Tagged its first stable release this week, v1.0.0 on November 24 followed by v1.0.1 on November 25, after nearly a year as a research preview. The most-starred repo this lane has tracked.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0. A research framework, not a live trading system with enforceable limits; star count is a checked snapshot, not a trend rank or evidence of returns. Not installed or tested.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: vAPI-Network/vapi-network
repoPicks.summary: A buyer-controlled client for x402 API payments in USDC on Base, giving an agent one wallet per paid call.
repoPicks.why: Created in October and still committing through November 27; buyer-side control of x402 payments is the half of the protocol this lane's security notes keep pointing at.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0. Client-side control helps the buyer but is not custodian-side enforcement, the limit called out in this week's Pakt entry. Not installed or tested.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick

repoPicks.name: valory-xyz/onchainbench
repoPicks.summary: The open benchmark behind this week's Valory announcement: tasks that test how safely and reliably AI agents operate crypto wallets.
repoPicks.why: Included because the artifact matters more than the count: the benchmark's tasks and methodology are worth reading alongside its announcement, and the honest snapshot is three stars as of this check.
repoPicks.caveat: Apache-2.0, created November 19. Methodology is self-published and results are vendor-reported; near-zero adoption so far. Not installed or tested.
repoPicks.label: Notable open-source / editorial pick
